name: Manali
description: Manali is a high-altitude hill station in the Kullu Valley sitting at roughly 2,050 metres, serving as a gateway to Lahaul-Spiti, Leh, and the Rohtang Pass. It draws a wide mix of travelers — honeymooners, trekkers, bikers heading to Ladakh, and families — though the main bazaar can feel crowded and commercialised in peak summer. The surrounding valleys, apple orchards, and high passes reward those willing to venture beyond the town centre.
nearest_railhead: Joginder Nagar Railway Station (160 km) — most travelers use Chandigarh or Pathankot and take a bus/taxi from there
nearest_airport: Bhuntar Airport (Kullu-Manali Airport), approximately 50 km south of Manali town

attractions.name: Rohtang Pass
attractions.description: A high mountain pass at 3,978 metres on the Kullu-Lahaul border, offering snow even in summer and dramatic Himalayan views. The road is frequently congested with tourist vehicles and requires an entry permit; the experience can feel crowded but the landscape is genuinely spectacular.

attractions.name: Solang Valley
attractions.description: A broad glacial valley about 14 km north of Manali, popular for paragliding, zorbing, and skiing in winter. Gets very crowded in May–June; the adventure activities are commercially run and pricey, but the valley itself is beautiful and accessible.

attractions.name: Hadimba Temple (Dhungri Temple)
attractions.description: A 16th-century wooden pagoda-style temple set inside a cedar forest, dedicated to the goddess Hadimba from the Mahabharata. The craftsmanship on the carved wooden doorway is impressive; the surrounding deodar grove is peaceful in the early hours before tourist crowds arrive.

attractions.name: Old Manali Village
attractions.description: The original village settlement across the Manalsu stream from the main bazaar, retaining traditional Himachali stone-and-wood houses alongside backpacker cafes. Worth an afternoon stroll to see the Manu Maharishi Temple and the slower pace of village life, though it has become progressively more tourist-oriented over the years.

attractions.name: Vashisht Village and Hot Springs
attractions.description: A village 3 km from Manali town with natural sulphur hot springs channelled into public and private bathing tanks, along with the ancient Vashisht temple. The spring water is genuinely hot and reputed to have therapeutic properties; the public baths are basic but authentic.

attractions.name: Naggar Castle
attractions.description: A 15th-century castle built in traditional Himachali timber-and-stone style by Raja Sidh Singh, now partly converted into a heritage hotel. Sitting on a ridge above the Beas River with wide valley views, Naggar is quieter than Manali and makes for a rewarding half-day excursion or an alternative base.

attractions.name: Beas Kund Trek
attractions.description: A two-to-three day moderate trek from Solang Valley to the glacial source lake of the Beas River at 3,700 metres, passing through alpine meadows and moraines. Relatively accessible for fit beginners and rewards with clear-day views of Hanuman Tibba and Shitidhar peaks; trail can be icy early in the season.

attractions.name: Nicholas Roerich Art Gallery, Naggar
attractions.description: The former home and studio of Russian artist Nicholas Roerich in Naggar, displaying original paintings and personal artefacts in a well-maintained heritage building. A genuinely undervisited gem; Roerich's Himalayan landscapes are striking and the hilltop setting adds to the atmosphere.

attractions.name: Chandrakhani Pass Trek
attractions.description: A challenging day-hike or overnight trek from Naggar village to a 3,660-metre pass that opens up panoramic views of the Kullu Valley and the snow peaks of Deo Tibba. Far less trafficked than the Rohtang route and genuinely rewarding; trail starts through dense forest before breaking into high meadows.

attractions.name: Jagatsukh and Deo Tibba Base Camp approach
attractions.description: The ancient village of Jagatsukh, once the capital of Kullu, sits 6 km south of Manali and is a trailhead for the multi-day trek toward Deo Tibba base camp. The village itself has 8th-century Shiva and Gauri Shankar temples carved in Pratihara style — almost entirely missed by mainstream tourists.
